#!/usr/bin/env bash
# WorktreeCreate / WorktreeRemove hook dispatch.
# Wired in .claude/settings.json for both events.
# Subcommands: create | remove | probe.

set -euo pipefail

# Force the MAIN checkout root, not the current toplevel: the WorktreeRemove
# hook runs with cwd INSIDE the worktree being removed (probe 2026-07-07),
# where --show-toplevel returns the worktree root and every .worktrees/ path
# below would silently mis-resolve. The common git dir always lives in the
# main checkout.
cd "$(dirname "$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir)")"

payload=$(cat)

NAME_REGEX='^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$'

die() {
  echo "worktree.sh: $*" >&2
  exit 1
}

command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "jq is required"

validate_name() {
  local n="$1"
  [[ -n "$n" ]] || die "name is empty"
  [[ "$n" =~ $NAME_REGEX ]] || die "name '$n' fails validation"
  [[ "$n" != *..* ]] || die "name '$n' contains '..'"
}

cmd_create() {
  local name
  name=$(jq -r '.name // empty' <<<"$payload")
  validate_name "$name"

  mkdir -p .worktrees

  local dir=".worktrees/${name}"
  local branch="worktree-${name}"

  git worktree add "$dir" -b "$branch" >&2

  # Docs: .worktreeinclude is bypassed under a custom WorktreeCreate hook.
  # https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees
  if [[ -f .worktreeinclude ]]; then
    git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-from=.worktreeinclude -z \
      | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
          mkdir -p "$dir/$(dirname "$f")"
          cp "$f" "$dir/$f"
        done
  fi

  realpath "$dir"
}

cmd_remove() {
  # WorktreeRemove stdin schema (docs.claude.com): `.worktree_path` is the
  # canonical absolute-path field. Older / undocumented variants used
  # `.path`; keep it as a fallback before deriving from `.name`.
  local path
  path=$(jq -r '.worktree_path // .path // empty' <<<"$payload")
  if [[ -z "$path" ]]; then
    local name
    name=$(jq -r '.name // empty' <<<"$payload")
    [[ -n "$name" ]] || die "WorktreeRemove payload missing both .path and .name"
    validate_name "$name"
    path=".worktrees/${name}"
  fi

  if [[ ! -d "$path" ]]; then
    echo "worktree.sh: nothing to remove at $path" >&2
    exit 0
  fi

  # Refuse to delete a live process's cwd — that breaks every later command
  # spawn in the occupying session (ENOENT posix_spawn '/bin/sh'). The
  # occupancy engine excludes this hook's own process lineage, so a
  # legitimate auto-clean (whose cwd sits inside the worktree being removed)
  # does not deadlock; only OTHER sessions' processes block. The hook owns
  # removal (replace semantics, probed 2026-07-07): a non-zero exit here
  # aborts the harness removal entirely, so failing is safe.
  local python_bin script_dir abs_path occupants occupancy_status
  python_bin="$(command -v python3 || command -v python)" \
    || die "python3/python is required for the occupancy check"
  script_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd -P)"
  abs_path="$(cd "$path" && pwd -P)" || die "cannot resolve '$path'"
  occupancy_status=0
  occupants="$("$python_bin" "$script_dir/worktree-occupancy.py" --occupancy "$abs_path")" \
    || occupancy_status=$?
  if [[ $occupancy_status -ne 0 ]]; then
    die "could not verify occupancy of '$path' (exit $occupancy_status); refusing removal"
  fi
  if [[ -n "$occupants" && "${WORKTREE_REMOVE_ALLOW_OCCUPIED:-0}" != "1" ]]; then
    die "refusing to remove occupied worktree '$path' — live occupants (pid/command/cwd):
$occupants
Exit the occupying session or kill the PIDs, then retry, or re-run with
WORKTREE_REMOVE_ALLOW_OCCUPIED=1 to override."
  fi

  git worktree remove "$path" >&2 || die "git worktree remove '$path' failed"

  # Best-effort branch cleanup — delete only fully-merged branches. `-d`
  # refuses unmerged branches; `|| true` swallows the refusal so the hook
  # never fails. Never force-delete here — a stale convention branch with
  # unmerged commits shouldn't lose work when its worktree is removed.
  local branch="worktree-$(basename "$path")"
  if git show-ref --quiet "refs/heads/$branch"; then
    git branch -d "$branch" >&2 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
}

cmd_probe() {
  # Diagnostic: capture stdin to disk while WorktreeRemove schema is undocumented.
  local out
  out="/tmp/worktree-probe-$(date +%s).json"
  printf '%s\n' "$payload" >"$out"
  echo "worktree.sh: probe payload at $out" >&2
}

case "${1:-}" in
  create) cmd_create ;;
  remove) cmd_remove ;;
  probe)  cmd_probe ;;
  *) die "usage: worktree.sh {create|remove|probe}" ;;
esac

--- title: "Release notes — v0.9 🚀" tags: [desktop, daemon] draft: false --- # Release notes The daemon now colors code **once** and every surface paints the *same* spans. See `highlight.read` and the [ADR](../decisions/033.md) for why. ## What changed 1. Spans travel as classes, never colors. 2. A theme switch repaints in place — no flash. - Nested item with `inline code` and __bold__ text. - Another with _emphasis_ and ~~strike~~. > A quote that holds a fence: > > ```ts > export const answer: number = 42; // the answer > ``` ### TypeScript ```typescript interface Span { offset: number; length: number; kind: "keyword" | "name" } export function pack(spans: readonly Span[]): number[] { return spans.flatMap((s) => [s.offset, s.length, s.kind === "keyword" ? 0 : 1]); } ``` ### SQL ```sql CREATE TABLE "notes" (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, body TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'café'); SELECT id, body FROM notes WHERE id > 10 ORDER BY id DESC; ``` ### Python ```python def fold(text: str) -> str: """Case-fold for matching.""" return text.casefold().strip() # naïve 🐍 ``` ### Shell ```bash for f in *.md; do echo "checking $f"; done && exit 0 ``` ### JSON and YAML ```json { "name": "sidekicks", "version": "0.9.0", "private": true, "count": 3 } ``` ```yaml on: [push] jobs: test: { runs-on: ubuntu-latest, timeout-minutes: 10 } ``` ### Rust and Go ```rust fn main() { let n: u32 = 7; println!("{n} 🦀"); } ``` ```go func Add(a, b int) int { return a + b } ``` ### A diff ```diff --- a/run.ts +++ b/run.ts @@ -1,3 +1,3 @@ -const limit = 10; +const limit = 20; export { limit }; ``` ### Markup ```html

yaml.source:
# Doc-corpus integrity CI: two checks and one aggregator.
#
#   1. lychee-inbound: `file://` and anchor integrity, offline. It catches a PR that breaks a
#      `[text](./file.md#anchor)` cite. Required via docs-corpus-gate and path-filtered, so a PR
#      touching no markdown skips it.
#   2. lychee-outbound: outbound HTTP probe, online. Third-party drift and link rot we do not own
#      (WAFs rejecting bot user agents, remotes timing out). It runs weekly, never on a PR, and
#      files an issue when it finds rot. The split follows the error model: an outbound failure is a
#      third-party server misbehaving; an inbound failure is a broken anchor the PR introduced.
#
# Branch protection on main requires only the `docs-corpus-gate` job; develop requires no check.
# Individual jobs are not stable required-check targets; the aggregator is. The gate treats a
# skipped job as success, so a path filter never leaves it pending.
#
# The lychee install is duplicated across the two jobs (inline curl plus a sha256 check against the
# musl-static asset). Keep the two `LYCHEE_VERSION` constants in sync.

name: docs-corpus

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [develop, main]
  push:
    branches: [develop, main]
  schedule:
    # Weekly outbound link-rot sweep. Nothing else in this workflow runs on it.
    - cron: "0 6 * * 1"

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.head_ref || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  # Did this event touch anything the corpus checks read? A workflow-level
  # `paths:` filter would suppress the check entirely, which a required check on
  # `main` reads as permanently pending; a job-level `if:` reports `skipped`,
  # which the aggregator accepts.
  changes:
    name: changed paths
    # The weekly sweep runs only lychee-outbound, which reads nothing here.
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      # `|| 'true'` is the off-pull-request default: the filter step runs only
      # where a base ref gives it a diff to classify, so a push does the full
      # sweep.
      docs: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.docs || 'true' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - id: filter
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        uses: dorny/paths-filter@0e4a8c6effa4802afeda77dc8d303f8176d7dfad # v3
        with:
          filters: |
            docs:
              - '**/*.md'
              - '.lychee.toml'
              # A PR that changes only the lychee install or the check command
              # must run them; the weekly schedule runs lychee-outbound alone,
              # so nothing else would catch a broken inbound gate.
              - '.github/workflows/docs-corpus.yml'

  lychee-inbound:
    name: lychee — inbound anchors (required)
    needs: [changes]
    # A push to `main` always sweeps, whatever the diff touched: it is the
    # branch whose protection names this workflow's gate. On a pull request
    # `github.ref` is the merge ref, so the filter alone decides there.
    if: needs.changes.outputs.docs == 'true' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v5

      # Inline install, pinned to v0.24.2, musl-static, SHA256-verified.
      # `lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2` is broken for v0.24.x: its install script
      # runs `tar -xvzf` without `--strip-components=1` and the binary lands at
      # `lychee-<triple>/lychee` instead of the flat `lychee` it then installs.
      # Keep `LYCHEE_VERSION` here in sync with the lychee-outbound job below.
      - name: Install lychee v0.24.2
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          LYCHEE_VERSION="v0.24.2"
          BASE="https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee/releases/download/lychee-${LYCHEE_VERSION}"
          ASSET="lychee-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz"
          curl -fsSL "${BASE}/${ASSET}" -o /tmp/lychee.tar.gz
          curl -fsSL "${BASE}/${ASSET}.sha256" -o /tmp/lychee.sha256
          EXPECTED=$(awk '{print $1}' /tmp/lychee.sha256)
          ACTUAL=$(sha256sum /tmp/lychee.tar.gz | awk '{print $1}')
          if [ "${EXPECTED}" != "${ACTUAL}" ]; then
            echo "SHA256 mismatch: expected ${EXPECTED}, got ${ACTUAL}" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p "${HOME}/.local/bin"
          tar -xzf /tmp/lychee.tar.gz -C "${HOME}/.local/bin" --strip-components=1
          chmod +x "${HOME}/.local/bin/lychee"
          echo "${HOME}/.local/bin" >> "${GITHUB_PATH}"

      - name: Run lychee (offline — inbound file refs + anchors)
        # file:// resolution + anchor checks (`include_fragments = "full"`
        # from `.lychee.toml`). This is the PR-introduced regression we own: a
        # broken `[text](./file.md#anchor)` cite from a code or doc edit fails
        # here. Pre-commit runs no link check — it is too slow to sit in front
        # of every commit — so this is the only place the invariant is verified.
        run: |
          lychee --offline --no-progress --config .lychee.toml './**/*.md'

  lychee-outbound:
    name: lychee — outbound HTTP (weekly)
    # Weekly only: a third-party 502 is not caused by the PR it appears on and its author cannot fix
    # it. On a schedule the finding becomes an issue with an owner and a log.
    if: github.event_name == 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      # `gh issue create` below is the job's product.
      issues: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v5

      # Inline install, pinned to v0.24.2, musl-static, SHA256-verified.
      # `lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2` is broken for v0.24.x: its install script
      # runs `tar -xvzf` without `--strip-components=1` and the binary lands at
      # `lychee-<triple>/lychee` instead of the flat `lychee` it then installs.
      # Keep `LYCHEE_VERSION` here in sync with the lychee-inbound job above.
      - name: Install lychee v0.24.2
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          LYCHEE_VERSION="v0.24.2"
          BASE="https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee/releases/download/lychee-${LYCHEE_VERSION}"
          ASSET="lychee-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz"
          curl -fsSL "${BASE}/${ASSET}" -o /tmp/lychee.tar.gz
          curl -fsSL "${BASE}/${ASSET}.sha256" -o /tmp/lychee.sha256
          EXPECTED=$(awk '{print $1}' /tmp/lychee.sha256)
          ACTUAL=$(sha256sum /tmp/lychee.tar.gz | awk '{print $1}')
          if [ "${EXPECTED}" != "${ACTUAL}" ]; then
            echo "SHA256 mismatch: expected ${EXPECTED}, got ${ACTUAL}" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p "${HOME}/.local/bin"
          tar -xzf /tmp/lychee.tar.gz -C "${HOME}/.local/bin" --strip-components=1
          chmod +x "${HOME}/.local/bin/lychee"
          echo "${HOME}/.local/bin" >> "${GITHUB_PATH}"

      - name: Run lychee (online — outbound HTTP probes) and file an issue on rot
        # Whole-repo HTTP probe for outbound link rot. `--include-fragments=none` disables anchor
        # checking on fetched pages, because anchors on JS-rendered third-party docs are not in the
        # static HTML lychee parses. Inbound `file.md#anchor` checks are the offline pass in
        # `lychee-inbound`. The accept-list (200..=299 and 429) lives in `.lychee.toml` so any
        # runner applies the same policy.
        #
        # One outer retry after a 15s pause absorbs whole-run flakes (a DNS hiccup or dropped packet
        # retries every URL together, beyond lychee's per-URL `max_retries`) and still surfaces real
        # rot when both passes agree.
        #
        # The step exits 0 after filing the issue: the issue is the signal, and a red weekly run
        # nobody owns is noise.
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          attempt() {
            lychee --no-progress --config .lychee.toml --include-fragments=none './**/*.md' \
              2>&1 | tee -a "${RUNNER_TEMP}/lychee-outbound.log"
            return "${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
          }
          : > "${RUNNER_TEMP}/lychee-outbound.log"
          if attempt; then
            echo "ok: no outbound link rot"
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "lychee online pass failed; retrying once after 15s to absorb runner-network flakes" >&2
          sleep 15
          : > "${RUNNER_TEMP}/lychee-outbound.log"
          if attempt; then
            echo "ok: no outbound link rot (second attempt)"
            exit 0
          fi
          {
            echo "The weekly outbound link sweep found broken external links."
            echo
            echo "Run: ${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
            echo
            echo '```'
            # Bounded so a wholesale outage cannot exceed the issue-body limit;
            # the full log is in the run linked above.
            tail -c 50000 "${RUNNER_TEMP}/lychee-outbound.log"
            echo '```'
          } > "${RUNNER_TEMP}/issue-body.md"
          gh issue create \
            --title "Outbound link rot: weekly lychee sweep $(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)" \
            --body-file "${RUNNER_TEMP}/issue-body.md"
          echo "::warning title=lychee outbound rot::Outbound HTTP probe found broken external links; an issue was filed."

  docs-corpus-gate:
    name: docs-corpus-gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [changes, lychee-inbound]
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Aggregate required-checks status
        # One predicate for every job: `skipped` counts as success, so a path-filtered job that did
        # not need to run cannot hold the gate pending. `cancelled` and `failure` are not accepted
        # and still fail.
        #
        # `changes` is checked too: a path filter that errors skips every job that needs it,
        # indistinguishable from a filter miss, so without this line a broken filter would take
        # `lychee-inbound` with it and leave the gate green. On the weekly schedule `changes` is
        # legitimately skipped, which the helper accepts.
        run: |
          fail=0
          check() {
            if [[ "$2" != "success" && "$2" != "skipped" ]]; then
              echo "docs-corpus-gate: job '$1' did not succeed (result=$2)"
              fail=1
            fi
          }
          check changes "${{ needs.changes.result }}"
          check lychee-inbound "${{ needs.lychee-inbound.result }}"
          if [[ $fail -ne 0 ]]; then exit 1; fi
          echo "docs-corpus-gate: all required jobs succeeded or were skipped by path filter"
